a126.speaker: Isidore Hakizimana, legal representative of Acorec-Tunywane
a126.speech: States that it was on 13 December 2013 that the idea of setting up a framework for reflection and dialogue came to him, with the objective of countering everything that blocks the effective reconciliation of the Burundian people ; explains that reconciliation is a great challenge to be met given the painful events that have marked and continue to mark the country’s history ; acknowledges that his organisation alone can do nothing and urges the support of Burundians driven by the will to take a clear-eyed look at their past: “With its ups and downs, we must overcome it and move forward.”

a126.speaker: Brother Emmanuel Ntakarutimana, expert
a126.speech: Observes that the world is currently living through the great challenge of working to heal the wounds left by injustices, violence and wars; recounts that repeatedly accumulated traumas often lead to cycles of violence, with a vicious circle of oscillation between victims and executioners; continues that, with the accumulation of shocks left by different tragedies, the question arises of how humanity can reverse these trends to find mechanisms tending towards respect for life and the integrity of peoples ; warns that the question of reconciliation refers to a patient, slow and delicate process: “It is not the work of a single day.” Citing the Canadian psychologist Jean Monbourquette, he indicates that there are at least 12 stages to go through to arrive at forgiveness and reconciliation: “…The history of past ‘reconciliations’ between the Germans and the Poles, or between the Poles and the Jews, for example, shows us that the time required is not measured in months but in generations.” ; reassures that this is not meant to discourage Acorec, because in any case one must start one day and set minds in motion.

a126.speaker: Mgr Jean Louis Nahimana, President of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (CVR)
a126.speech: Says the role of the CVR is limited to investigations in order to establish the truth about what happened in the country from independence (1 July 1962) until 2008, the end of the belligerence; the CVR will have to clarify the context, identify the causes and circumstances in which the crimes were committed and draw up lists of the victims; he specifies that it will also be necessary to identify all the mass graves, organise the burial of the victims and erect monuments; according to him, once this work is completed, it will be the moment for forgiveness, reparation and reconciliation: “Transitional justice, as had been envisaged, is far from the CVR’s remit.” ; reassures that when the CVR begins its work, it will surprise people.

a126.speaker: Participants at the launch ceremony (debate)
a126.speech: In the view of most participants, the road to effective reconciliation is still long.

a163.speaker: Elhadj Mohamed Katty, Kountigui (traditional chief) of Boffa
a163.speech: Welcomed the pilgrims on behalf of the authorities and the population: "In the name of the citizens of Boffa, I welcome you to your home. Here, Christians and Muslims live in brotherhood and good coexistence. I invite the citizens of Boffa to house, feed and welcome their Christian brothers and sisters in their homes. Finally, I wish all the Christian faithful a good pilgrimage."

a163.speaker: Monseigneur Vincent Coulibaly, Archbishop
a163.speech: "Boffa is the gateway of the Christian faith in Guinea. It is here that the Church was welcomed for the first time. That is why, every year, we come here on pilgrimage. We very sincerely thank the authorities and the citizens of Boffa for their hospitality. In Boffa, we are welcomed like any Guinean. Throughout all our prayers, we prayed intensely for the country's authorities, for the politicians, so that there may be peace and social calm in Guinea. We are proud of Boffa, where Muslims and Christians coexist harmoniously. We ask God to grant peace to the prefecture of Boffa."

a163.speaker: Christine Bangoura, pilgrim
a163.speech: Expressed her joy: "it was an intense moment of contemplation and blessing for me. We walked from Fria to Boffa, and it was a moment of penitence. This is my second time taking part in the Boffa pilgrimage. I pray God to grant happiness in abundance to the prefecture of Boffa, which is the source of our Christian faith."

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of the UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC (MONUSCO)
a321.speech: Briefed journalists from Goma that “the situation is still highly volatile, with persistent risks of escalation,” emphasising that military action alone will not resolve the conflict.

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of MONUSCO
a321.speech: Warned that the peacekeeping mission was operating in an increasingly challenging environment: “The mission's key infrastructures in Goma are overwhelmed, with both UN personnel and Congolese seeking shelter within our premises,” with some 2,000 people on site and growing pressure on “critical resources” like water, food and sanitation.

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of MONUSCO
a321.speech: Said the mission was “gravely concerned” over Kavumu airport and the potential that it could be taken by rebel forces, warning that losing both airports “in the midst of an ongoing humanitarian and IDP crisis will be untenable” for the population of the region.

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of MONUSCO
a321.speech: Confirmed the presence of Rwandan forces in eastern DR Congo, despite denials from Kigali, saying the UN has restricted movement, limiting verification capabilities.

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of MONUSCO
a321.speech: Explained that the mission needs “clear guidance” from the Security Council, as the fluid situation is “changing literally every hour.”

a321.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Head of MONUSCO
a321.speech: Underscored the urgent need for a political solution: “The people of the DRC deserve peace, security and stability,” calling on all parties to “put an end to hostilities, prioritise dialogue and work towards a peaceful resolution.”

a321.speaker: MONUSCO (UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC)
a321.speech: Has confirmed that Goma airport continues to be under M23 control after their takeover last week and has suffered significant damage, including to the control tower, with UN personnel denied access to the site.

a321.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a321.speech: Now warns of potential disease outbreaks as bodies continue to be recovered across the city, with over 2,000 bodies already buried and 900 remaining in morgues.

a321.speaker: Government of Rwanda (Kigali)
a321.speech: Denies the presence of Rwandan forces in eastern DR Congo.

a321.speaker: Multiple reports (unnamed)
a321.speech: Have cited Rwandan military involvement alongside M23 ; further reports indicate that M23 has instructed NGOs to halt operations in areas under its control, limiting humanitarian access.

a321.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, UN Spokesperson
a321.speech: “We reiterate our call for the urgent reopening of Goma airport, as we need to evacuate wounded people and bring in humanitarian supplies and staff in.”

a433.speaker: Prof. Mariatou Kone, Ivorian Minister of National Education and Literacy
a433.speech: Indicated that for the 2023-2024 school year everything had been settled: "We are in 2024-2025, the commitments have also been made. But there is a gap of 92 billion and the State is doing everything possible to have it paid. I think we have understood each other. We left satisfied because there had been a communication deficit. The files that reached our level have been processed, transmitted and are in the process of being paid."

a433.speaker: Prof. Mariatou Kone, Ivorian Minister of National Education and Literacy
a433.speech: On the "fair debt" the State wants to pay: "In the name of this fair debt, we now have a biometric control system that some do not appreciate. That is the price to pay to reduce school fees for the State of Cote d'Ivoire."

a433.speaker: Prof. Mariatou Kone, Ivorian Minister of National Education and Literacy
a433.speech: Reassured parents about the holding of the major examinations: "There is no problem with the founders of private schools. This meeting takes place within the normal framework that we have, every year, with the various actors of the education system. For the moment, there is no problem."

a433.speaker: Prof. Mariatou Kone, Ivorian Minister of National Education and Literacy
a433.speech: Recalled that establishing direct dialogue between the ministry and the actors of the education system aims to create a calm school environment conducive to the smooth running of the school year and of learning, "with a view to better performance, particularly for the children taking part in the major examinations."

a433.speaker: Ibrahim Karamoko, President of the National Federation of Private Secular Schools of Cote d'Ivoire (Feneplaci)
a433.speech: Welcomed the minister's determination to give a favourable response to their concerns: "The minister assured us that she will carry our voice to the government so that these payments can be made. She indicated that she is working in that direction. We are happy that she is personally involved in settling the school fees." ; "We have educated children and our objective is to assess them. Only, to do that, the teachers and the staff must have money."

a512.speaker: Antoine Gerard, UN deputy humanitarian co-ordinator for Sudan
a512.speech: Told the BBC that a landslide has killed at least 370 people in the remote Marra Mountains in western Sudan, and said that it was hard to assess the scale of the incident or the exact death toll as the area was very hard to reach.

a512.speaker: Antoine Gerard, UN deputy humanitarian co-ordinator for Sudan
a512.speech: Said getting aid quickly to the area would be difficult: "We do not have helicopters, everything goes in vehicles on very bumpy roads. It takes time and it is the rainy season - sometimes we have to wait hours, maybe a day or two to cross a valley... bringing in trucks with commodities will be a challenge."

a512.speaker: Sudan Liberation Movement/Army (SLM/A) (statement)
a512.speech: Had earlier said as many as 1,000 people could have died, and said in a statement that days of heavy rain triggered the landslide on Sunday, which left just one survivor and "levelled" much of the village of Tarseen; the SLM/A has appealed for humanitarian assistance from the UN and other regional and international organisations.

a557.speaker: Victor Fidalgo, economist and international consultant, specialist in tourism
a557.speech: Spoke with Expresso das Ilhas about the economy for the year now beginning - the internal and external scenarios, the attraction of foreign direct investment or the lack of it, the rise in interest rates, diversification and tourism: "We are pleased with our growth rates and that is not good."

a652.speaker: Nathan Geffen, editor of GroundUp (opinion column)
a652.speech: writes that the world class research conducted in SA is vital for everyone; acknowledges there are severe criticisms to be made of US foreign aid — that it is often wasteful and almost always very bureaucratic, sometimes serves sinister interests such as when a vaccination project in Pakistan was used in the effort to catch Osama bin Laden, and that billions of dollars in US military aid go annually to Egypt and Israel, who use that aid to oppress people ; but argues that US aid, mostly for HIV in South Africa, and for food and health care in other African countries, has been very beneficial for these countries, as well as the US and the world, and that the withdrawal of this aid by President Donald Trump will damage not only Africa but the United States too.

a652.speaker: Nathan Geffen, editor of GroundUp (opinion column)
a652.speech: Argues that conducting health research in South Africa is a win-win for South Africa, the United States and the world, that at least two HIV vaccine trials are paused because of the suspension of US aid, and that a tuberculosis outbreak in Kansas is likely to be contained in part thanks to research on TB conducted in African countries funded by the US government ; concludes: “The withdrawal of US aid is a very hard knock for South Africa and catastrophic for some African countries, but the United States and the rest of the world also lose. Hopefully, sense will prevail, and the US government will restore PEPFAR and other aid that has been extremely beneficial to millions of people around the world, including American citizens.”

a652.speaker: Associated Press
a652.speech: reports that the shutdown of USAID is “upending livelihoods for nonprofit workers, farmers and other Americans” and that “US organisations do billions of dollars of business with USAID and the State Department, which oversee more than $60 billion in foreign assistance.”

a652.speaker: DevelopmentAid (aid data company)
a652.speech: According to the company, “More than 80% of companies that have contracts with USAID are American.”

a652.speaker: The START trial (results published 2015)
a652.speech: showed that people with HIV benefit from starting antiretroviral treatment as early in their infection as possible; it changed the management of HIV around the world, with nearly 4,700 patient volunteers across the world and South Africa contributing the most participants: 518.

a652.speaker: The HPTN 052 trial (final results published 2016)
a652.speech: showed that if people with HIV took antiretroviral medicines, there was almost no risk of passing the virus on to their HIV-negative partners; this too has informed HIV guidelines across the world.

a652.speaker: The PURPOSE-1 clinical trial
a652.speech: showed that a twice-yearly injection of a new drug gave women total protection from HIV; the trial was conducted in South Africa and Uganda.

a654.speaker: Paul Thelon, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to South Sudan
a654.speech: has commended the Dutch Relief Alliance for its dedication in delivering humanitarian aid in some of the world’s most challenging countries, including South Sudan, and praised the DRA for its impact on humanitarian policy and life-saving work globally: “I would like to commend you and compliment you for completing 10 years in delivering humanitarian aid in some of the world’s most challenging countries, South Sudan. Your dedication, your resilience and perseverance are a testament to your commitment to humanity.” ; said the alliance has become a trusted partner not only in South Sudan but also in many other countries ; added that the DRA is currently working with seven local organizations across South Sudan to help communities recover from conflict and address urgent needs, including access to food, clean water, sanitation, livelihoods, and economic empowerment through cash transfers.

a723.speaker: Country Directors of national and international humanitarian agencies working in Somalia (letter to UN Secretary-General António Guterres)
a723.speech: Sent a letter to the United Nations Secretary-General, António Guterres, to urge urgent action needed to avert a possible famine in Somalia in 2022: “We, the Country Directors of national and international humanitarian agencies working in Somalia, are writing to express our deepest concern at the possibility of famine in Somalia in 2022. The humanitarian situation is deteriorating rapidly, with about 4.5 million people in need of urgent humanitarian assistance due to the worsening drought conditions.” ; “What we are now seeing is impending famine similar to that which occurred in 2010/2011 in which more than a quarter of a million people died - including 133,000 children under the age of five. Although some donors have committed to fund Somalia’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) which seeks US$1.5 billion, not even 4% of funding required to meet Somalia’s humanitarian needs have been allocated.” ; “However, the international community has not yet grasped the urgency of the situation, which is deteriorating fast. We are concerned that Somalia’s possible famine is not high enough on the list of international disaster responses with focus now on the Ukrainian crisis. We request you to urge donors and the Member States to commit additional resources to enable immediate scale-up of humanitarian response in Somalia to avert a possible famine and save lives.” ; “We also request you to urge all stakeholders including the Somali Federal Government, Federal States and armed groups to allow access and speedy facilitation of delivery of the emergency humanitarian aid to the affected, and where possible, we also request you to urge talking to the other side (Al-Shabab) for humanitarian access.” ; “We are running out of time. It is time to keep the promise of ‘never again’ that was made during the 2017 drought when the immediate action of the humanitarian community led to lives being saved. The window to avert a famine is closing fast. If we don’t want to see history repeating itself, we cannot delay action any longer.”

a723.speaker: UNICEF
a723.speech: According to UNICEF, for "a severely acutely malnourished child, or severely wasted child, the risk of them dying from diseases such as measles or diarrhea is 11 times higher than for a well-nourished child."

a723.speaker: Weather experts
a723.speech: Forecast unprecedented fourth consecutive below-average rains during the long rainy season of April to June across most of the country.

a829.speaker: Eyewitnesses
a829.speech: Said the victim had just returned from church when he was killed and had gone to buy food at a Mobil Filling Station along Enugu-Abakaliki Road when the accident occurred; provided conflicting accounts of the cause of the accident, with some stating that the truck driver was sleeping, while others claimed that the truck veered off course after a Sienna vehicle made a sudden turn on the highway.

a829.speaker: One of the eyewitnesses (anonymous)
a829.speech: Told SaharaReporters: “The boy had already bought Okpa that the parents sent him to buy and was returning home when the unfortunately incident happened. He was walking on the pedestrian walkway and truck ran over him. His brother and two other persons narrowly survived. They have been taken to the hospital while the police have taken the deceased to the mortuary.”

a841.speaker: Abdulateef Shittu, Director General of Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF)
a841.speech: Has called on States with overbloated Civil service to take proactive steps by deploying some of the workers to areas where their services are highly needed for optimal performance ; Pointed out that some States have overbloated Civil service, adding that States do not need overbloated Civil Service to guarantee efficient service delivery ; "I want to throw a poser to all the Heads of Service here. You should start thinking about the overbloated Civil Service in your States. You have to start thinking of the major reforms across the bureaucracy in the Service. I know that a country is as great as its civil service. The states are as strong as their civil service. When the Civil service is not working for the overall development of States, then we will be having issues. As we speak today, there are many challenges in the workforce. I will not mention states. We have some states that have 50,000 workforce. Some have 52,000. You don't have to sack them, you can deploy them to the areas of need to optimise resources."

a841.speaker: Irene Karimi, State2State Chief of Party
a841.speech: Explained that in the past four years, the USAID State Accountability, Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) Activity has invested in various interventions across the seven partner States ; Reaffirmed that these interventions that have resulted in governance, public financial management and citizen engagement reforms should be sustained beyond State2State ; Revealed that one of the sustainability and institutionalisation vehicles introduced by State2State across the partner states is the State Transformation Committee (STC), with the Offices of the Head of Service in the States playing crucial roles in the successes recorded by the STCs.

a841.speaker: Irene Karimi, State2State Chief of Party
a841.speech: On the essence of the Community of Practice, explained that it would serve as an avenue that facilitates and promotes quality conversations and peer-learning among actors and stakeholders within the office of States Head of Service to engender and sustain a stronger civil service, delivering quality service within the Activity's priority sectors such as basic education, primary health care and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services in the seven partner States.

a841.speaker: Dr. Joe Abah, DAI Nigeria Country Director
a841.speech: Blamed some Governors for overbloated Civil service, adding that some governors often employ civil servants on political exigencies, rather than on the basis of needs ; Called for strong collaboration, experience sharing and best practices between the Federal and States Civil Service.

a841.speaker: Stanley Achonu, Deputy Chief of Party, USAID State2State Activity
a841.speech: In an interview with Daily Independent, explained that in the last four years the organisation has funded extensive reforms in the partner States of Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Bauchi, Ebonyi, Gombe, Kebbi, and Sokoto ; Stated that institutional capacities of these States have been built towards effective utilisation of resources, improved laws and policies as well as deployment of resources to the priority sectors of education, healthcare, water, sanitation and hygiene ; Noted that many civil servants in these States have been trained in planning, procurement, internal audit, financial control, internally revenue generation and improvement ; Pointed out that these reforms would be sustainable if those who have been trained by USAID State2State are allowed to use their training and capacities to implement these reforms ; "What we are doing with CoP is to make sure that those who are custodians of the deployment of servants and human resources within the states are aware of the capacity which these people have received as well as the need to keep them in the relevant MDAs where they will continue to use the skills that we have given them to drive the reforms."

a910.speaker: Department of State Services (DSS) (petition letter signed by B. Bamigboye for the Director-General)
a910.speech: Asked X, formerly known as Twitter, to deactivate the account of Omoyele Sowore and gave the platform 24 hours to act, threatening “to take far-reaching, sweeping and across-the-board measures” if the social media platform failed to heed its request ; “We detected and monitored with dismay and consternation a widely condemned publication/trending Tweet by Omoyele Sowore on his X official handle page @YeleSowore on 25th August, 2025 about 11:38 PM local time (2338 hours) WAT disparaging and ridiculing the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” ; “Those words were personally directed at Mr. President through his official communication channel @officialABAT which is the known X handle of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” ; “The said tweet is still in circulation and has attracted widespread condemnation by majority of Nigerians, some of whom may resort to unwholesome activities to vent their grievance over it, especially supporters of the President who have started taking to the streets in protest, thereby creating political tension and threatening the country’s national security.” ; “under the Nigerian Law, these quoted tweets/words constitute offence punishable in Section 51 of the Criminal Code Act Cap.77 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, which prohibits publication of false information; Sections 19,22 and 24 of the Cyber Crimes Act 2025... amounting to domestic terrorism.” ; “It is against the above highlighted backdrop that we make an immediate and urgent demand on your Corporation to as a matter of its own policy, immediately TAKE DOWN the tweet and its attendant re-tweets. This demand is unequivocal with its attendant consequence. Should you fail, neglect and refuse to comply with the command in this notice, the Federal Government will be compelled to take far-reaching, sweeping and across-the-board measures through our Organization, whose mandate covers such criminal acts.”

a910.speaker: Omoyele Sowore, publisher and former Presidential Candidate (X/Twitter post, quoted in the DSS petition)
a910.speech: “This criminal @officialABAT actually went to Brazil to state that there is NO MORE corruption under his regime in Nigeria. What audacity to lie shamelessly!”

a910.speaker: Omoyele Sowore, publisher and former Presidential Candidate (non-response)
a910.speech: Sowore, known for taking a hard stance against the government, had not replied to this request as of the time of filing this report.

a933.speaker: Christian Youths in Politics of the People's Democratic Party (PDP), Bauchi State chapter
a933.speech: Have endorsed Honourable Faruq Mustapha for the position of Bauchi State governor in 2027.

a933.speaker: Comrade Jondes James, Chairman of the Christian Youths in Politics, PDP Bauchi State chapter
a933.speech: Said at a press conference that the group endorsed Hon Mustapha as the candidate of the PDP for Governor of Bauchi State in 2027 because he possesses all the needed leadership skills, vision, aura and integrity to transform Bauchi state and improve the lives of the citizens ; said that if given the mandate, Hon Mustapha will consolidate on the tremendous democracy dividends so far recorded by Governor Bala Mohammed ; said that given his quality and experience as an elite politician, banker, two-term member of the House of Representatives, DG Campaign for Governor Bala Mohammed's continuity in 2023 and serving commissioner for Rural Development and Special Duties, Hon Mustapha will not disappoint the people of the state if voted as governor in 2027 ; commended the commissioner's unique character and high spirit of accommodation, which cuts across all the existing religious faiths, and his commitment to good governance, transparency and accountability, and enjoined the people of Bauchi state to support the movement.

a933.speaker: Christian Youths in Politics of the People's Democratic Party (PDP), Bauchi State chapter
a933.speech: “We are confident that he will work tirelessly to ensure that Bauchi state is governed in the best interests of all its citizens. The group is impressed by Hon Faruq Mustapha's track record of service to the community and his ability to bring people together to achieve common goals” ; “His leadership style is characterized by inclusiveness, empathy, and a willingness to listen, which will be essential in building a government that truly serves the people” ; “Hon Faruq Mustapha will prioritize the development of our state's infrastructure, education, healthcare, and economy. He will work to create opportunities for our youth, empower our women, and ensure that our state is a place where everyone can thrive.”

a933.speaker: Comrade Jondes James, Chairman of the Christian Youths in Politics, PDP Bauchi State chapter
a933.speech: Appealed to Governor Bala Mohammed and the PDP leadership to consider zoning the PDP governorship ticket to Bauchi North Senatorial district and to consider Hon Faruq Mustapha as the befitting candidate, in the spirit of equity, fairness and justice: “We also call on all well-meaning Bauchi people to join in supporting Hon Faruq Mustapha's candidacy in 2027, because together, we can build a brighter future for our state and ensure that our government truly serves the people.”

a944.speaker: Choguel Maïga, Malian Prime Minister and chairman of the strategic committee of the M5-RFP
a944.speech: In a thunderous outburst on Saturday 16 November, at the rally commemorating the recapture of the capital of the Ifoghas from the CMA, did not mince his words, castigating his employers without restraint.

a944.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a944.speech: According to our sources, his departure, announced and postponed many times, is this time well and truly settled; from the same sources, the head of state had even informed him of it the day after his elevation to the dignity of Grand Officer of the National Order of Mali, a distinction which, our source adds, was only a way for the head of state to pay tribute to him for the three years spent at the head of the Government; he is protected, according to our sources, by one of the Generals.

a944.speaker: Associates of Choguel Maïga
a944.speech: maintain that, just like the military, he has not been unworthy and played a leading role in the coming of the Transition, and that it is therefore unacceptable that he should step aside in favour of eleventh-hour performers.

a1007.speaker: Herodotus, ancient Greek historian (484-425 BC)
a1007.speech: "They have a sort of hemp growing in this country (Scythia), very like flax, except in thickness and height; in this respect the hemp is far superior: it grows both spontaneously and from cultivation ..."

a1007.speaker: Helen Suzman, leader of South Africa's apartheid-era political opposition
a1007.speech: "I was the only MP in 1971 who voted against the so-called 'harshest drugs law in the world,'" she recalled in the months before her death. "[It was] introduced by the then-minister of welfare Connie Mulder ... The mandatory sentence was two years' imprisonment for possession of cannabis, or 'dagga,' and five years for being deemed a peddler. You were deemed a peddler if you had 115 grams in your possession."

a1007.speaker: Cannabis Acceptance Legalisation Movement (Calm), online video campaign
a1007.speech: The segment opens with a written statement asserting that the initial outlawing of cannabis in South Africa, back in 1870, was "inherently racist, aimed at controlling indentured Indian labour and black mine workers" ; insisted that South Africa's criminal justice system "cannot cope with serious crime let alone prosecuting cannabis use", acknowledged that there were no government statistics available on drug user arrests or the cost of the war on drugs but nonetheless estimated that taxpayers coughed up around R284-million to arrest and process 9% of those caught in a 2013 Drug Watch crackdown in Gauteng ; ended off with these words: "Recent cannabis crop spraying in the Eastern Cape is a health hazard that contaminates water sources, destroys livelihoods and [ruins] domestic food crops of the rural poor."

a1007.speaker: South African Police Service
a1007.speech: The police claimed the dose [of the herbicide Kilo Max sprayed on 500 hectares of cannabis fields in the Wild Coast region] was harmless and minimal.

a1007.speaker: Eyewitness reports by journalists and other interested parties
a1007.speech: Claimed otherwise: maize crops destroyed, locals falling ill, goats having miscarriages after drinking contaminated water.

a1007.speaker: Tony Budden, of the hemp retail chain Hemporium, one of South Africa's leading authorities on the cannabis plant
a1007.speech: "The spraying is paid for by the United Nations. It's foreign aid, part of our commitment to the war on drugs. We are being dictated to, go have a look at where this glyphosate comes from."

a1007.speaker: Tony Budden, of the hemp retail chain Hemporium
a1007.speech: "We know the industrial value of hemp," he said, "many governments across the world have proved what a boost it can be to their economies. We started this business in 1996, and we never dreamed that 20 years later we would still be importing fabric from China, twine from Germany, paper from Spain, 'hempcrete' from the UK." ; He said the South African government had held hemp in the 'research phase' for almost as long as he had been in business, and that it had been demonstrated time and again that the tetrahydrocannabinol content was well below the legal limit in the species under investigation ; He also noted that the state of Colorado in the US, which legalised marijuana use in 2014, had by March this year generated $15-million in tax revenue for its public schools, and that Canada exported $48-million worth of hemp seeds in 2014.

a1007.speaker: Tony Budden, of the hemp retail chain Hemporium
a1007.speech: "The closer you get to the equator," he said, "the longer cannabis takes to mature. The Malawi variants are awesome, but they take eight months to mature. The Eastern Cape plants, with the added benefit of summer rainfall, take between five and six months."

a1007.speaker: Scientists funded by companies linked to Monsanto
a1007.speech: Have reams of data to prove that glyphosate is as safe as houses.

a1007.speaker: Paul-Michael Keichel, attorney of the legal firm Schindlers
a1007.speech: "All of the pleadings are in. At this point we are working very hard on securing our expert witnesses. We have just secured Dr Donald Abrams."

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: “At that time, most of the good schools and teachers were concentrated in the Greater Banjul Area, leaving students in rural communities to figure things out independently.”

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: notes of the students he taught as a Teaching Assistant at the University of The Gambia that some are “now doing great things.”

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: explained of his Ph.D. work on solar energy efficiency, “With fossil fuel depletion projected by 2060, solar energy is becoming more crucial.”

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: “When I got the job offer, I knew this was a once-in-a-lifetime chance.”

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: champions greater investment in homegrown tech solutions, warning that the continent's resources and digital future depend on it: “Technology is advancing rapidly, and Africa must not be left behind,” calling for more researchers to safeguard economic and data security.

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: “Not every deserving student will get a scholarship, but that should never be a reason to give up. Stay prepared, work hard, and always be ready for your opportunity.”

a1044.speaker: Ebrima Tunkara, scientist at Intel Corporation
a1044.speech: credits his work ethic, adaptability, and leadership for his achievements, envisions a future where Gambian students gain early exposure to STEM through university partnerships and hands-on research, and stresses the value of soft skills — communication and teamwork — alongside technical prowess as keys to thriving in tech.

a1105.speaker: International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation
a1105.speech: Announced at its virtual meeting on 13 June the formation of an international working group specialising in applications of artificial intelligence in search and rescue satellite systems.

a1105.speaker: United Arab Emirates National Guard, represented by the National Search and Rescue Center (working document)
a1105.speech: Presented a working document to the meetings of the international committee, putting forward a pioneering technical proposal aimed at integrating artificial intelligence technologies into Mission Control Center (MCC) operations, improving the efficiency of space rescue systems and improving the speed and accuracy of responding to emergency calls through intelligent data processing and integration across satellite networks.

a1105.speaker: Member states of the International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation
a1105.speech: Gave the UAE initiative broad praise for its innovation and forward-looking approach, reflecting the country's readiness and leadership in supporting international efforts to modernise the technical infrastructure of the COSPAS-SARSAT system.

a1105.speaker: International Committee on Artificial Intelligence in Search and Rescue Systems (recommendation)
a1105.speech: Adopted a recommendation to form a joint working group led by the UAE, to coordinate technical cooperation between member states and relevant authorities and develop artificial intelligence tools linked to mission control centres, thereby improving preparedness and responsiveness in search and rescue systems globally.

a1105.speaker: The Committee
a1105.speech: Praised the UAE's role, its qualitative contributions and its proactive initiatives in connection with the application of modern technologies to serve international humanitarian rescue objectives.

a1114.speaker: African Water and Sanitation Association (AAEA) (appeal)
a1114.speech: The AAEA issues an appeal to actors in the sector, to governments and to private and public organisations in order to build a sustainable future for Africa: every drop of water must become a vehicle of progress, every action a lever for harmonious development. The association therefore invites all those who wish to commit to effective and sustainable management of water and sanitation to join this drive.

a1154.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account – Benin (letter of invitation No. 432/08/MCA/DAF/DPM/DPASF/RCGF)
a1154.speech: Invites any concerned and interested structure or institution to submit project proposals in accordance with the terms of reference in annex 1; states that the MCC and the Government of the Republic of Benin have concluded a Millennium Challenge Account Grant Agreement of an amount not to exceed US$307,298,040 to foster economic development and reduce poverty; that MCA-Benin aims to combat poverty by accelerating economic growth; that the Facility's mission is to promote sustainable access for a greater number of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to adapted, lower-cost financial and non-financial services; that the total amount available under the Facility's grants is US$10.7 million (about 4.430 billion CFA francs), allocated competitively for projects of US$25,000 to US$250,000 (up to US$500,000 for consortia of a maximum of 10 institutions); and that proposals must be submitted in sealed envelopes against receipt from Tuesday 2 September 2008 to Friday 3 October 2008 at 12:00 noon.

a1154.speaker: Simon-Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1154.speech: Signed the letter of invitation, closing: "Veuillez agréer, Mesdames et Messieurs, l'expression de mes sentiments distingués" ("Yours faithfully").

a1154.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) — General Rules of Ethics of MCA-Benin
a1154.speech: Requires that MCA-Benin (including the beneficiaries of MCC Funds), as well as suppliers, companies and bidders under MCC-financed contracts, comply with the strictest rules of professional ethics during the procurement and execution of those contracts, and defines corruption, fraudulent practices, collusive practices, coercive practices, prohibited practices and obstructive practice; states that MCA-Benin will reject the proposal for award if the recommended bidder has engaged in such acts, may sanction a bidder or individual by excluding them indefinitely or for a fixed period from any MCC-financed contract, and shall have the right to require audit and inspection clauses; and that MCC will cancel the portion of MCC Funds allocated to the Contract if it establishes that a representative of the beneficiary engaged in such practices.

a1337.speaker: Embassy of the State of Palestine in Nigeria (statement issued Thursday)
a1337.speech: Lamented that thousands of Palestinian refugees and students in Gaza will suffer and probably die following the Israeli Knesset's approved bill to end the activities of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) in Gaza amid the ongoing war, and said that despite international opposition, the Israeli Knesset approved a bill to end UNRWA's activity in the occupied West Bank including East Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip.

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: Lamented that the decision would deepen the suffering and misery of millions of Palestinian refugees, especially in Gaza, adding that it would also deprive nearly 650,000 students of their right to education in Gaza alone. According to the Ambassador, UNRWA employs 30,000 Palestinians and serves almost six million refugees, including in Gaza where 1,476,706 Palestinians are registered as refugees in eight Palestinian refugee camps, while in the West Bank 800,000 are registered.

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: "This bill does not revoke the refugee status of Palestinians, as it is safeguarded by UNGA resolutions and many other international law instruments until their right to return is acknowledged and the question of Palestinian refugees is resolved by implementing UN Resolution 194."

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: "On the 391[st] day of the US-Israeli heinous, malicious, and vindictive genocide, here are some statistical figures: The death toll has risen to 43,163, with 101,510 injured." ; "As of October 30, for the 24th day in a row, the northern Gaza Strip has been completely cut off from the rest of the enclave, under a total siege with no access to humanitarian aid, medical assistance, supplies, water, and other basic necessities for life." ; "This has led to nearly 1000 martyrs, tens of missing persons and thousands injured, in addition to hundreds of homes being completely razed."

a1337.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1337.speech: Estimates that more than 60,000 people have been displaced in northern Gaza in October alone.

a1337.speaker: UNICEF
a1337.speech: Estimates that at least 19,000 children have been separated from their families, forced to fend for themselves; children are being medically evacuated from Gaza at a rate of fewer than one child per day.

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: "If this lethally slow pace continues, it would take more than seven years to evacuate the 2,500 children needing urgent medical care."

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: Noted that as of October 28, the total number of arrests has reached 11,500 in the Occupied West Bank, including Jerusalem, adding that the figures include 430 women, 750 children, and 132 journalists, with 59 of them still under arrest, including six women journalists and 31 journalists from Gaza ; "More than 9,392 administrative detainees have been reported. 41 prisoners were martyred, and their bodies are still being held captive."

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: "In Gaza only, at least 232 UNRWA staff have been killed. Over 200 UNRWA premises have been damaged or destroyed."

a1337.speaker: Israel Democracy Institute (survey)
a1337.speech: A survey published by the Israel Democracy Institute on the one-year anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack found that only 6% of Israelis think the war in Gaza should be stopped due to "the great cost in human life."

a1337.speaker: Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian Ambassador to Nigeria
a1337.speech: Noted that the international community raised a brilliant slogan called "We pledge that no one will be left behind," stressing, "We the Palestinians, were left behind."

a1374.speaker: The author's mother (a woman living with HIV, Uganda)
a1374.speech: Revealed to him when he was 11 that she was HIV positive; days before her death she called him to her bedside and said: "Take care of your siblings. I know... you are young but you will find a way." ; on hearing him sobbing, asked: "If you are crying now, where do you expect me to get the courage that I will be fine?"

a1374.speaker: Doctors at Mulago Hospital
a1374.speech: Said the severe headache from which the author's step-father died was meningitis.

a1374.speaker: Dr Stephen Watiti, HIV/AIDS activist
a1374.speech: "Things have changed. People now have a chance to live longer thanks to antiretroviral therapy."

a1374.speaker: Dr Stephen Watiti, HIV/AIDS activist
a1374.speech: Said that for the past two years donor funds have been scaled down because of the global financial crunch, yet there are more infections annually than the number of people who join the treatment line ; blamed the stagnation of Uganda's HIV prevalence at 6.4% for more than 10 years on complacency and normalisation: "Because we have managed to put many people back to work who would be dead by now, people think that AIDS is no longer a threat and that explains their reckless behaviour." ; advised: "We need to emphasise the ABC model (Abstinence, Be Faithful and Condom usage)... If we dont scale up the achievements we had attained, it would be like mopping a room while the tap is still running."

a1374.speaker: 2009 UNAIDS report
a1374.speech: "there are over 33.4 million infected persons in the world of which 1.3 [million] are Ugandans (4%)"; the report also "indicates a fall in new infection to 2.7 million people".

a1374.speaker: Anti-AIDS activists
a1374.speech: "argue that HIV patients have a right to live. Therefore denying them access to ARV treatment of any form is a violation of this fundamental human right."

a1374.speaker: Modes of Transmission study, led by Fred Wabwire Mangen, associate professor of epidemiology at Makerere University's School of Public Health
a1374.speech: Found that "new HIV/AIDS cases are increasingly occurring among married couples aged 30 to 40. The study further notes that about 650,000 Ugandans are unknowingly living with HIV-positive sexual partners and that almost 85,000 of these individuals or 13%, will contract the virus this year if nothing is done to increase awareness about the situation."

a1374.speaker: AIDS Control Programme (ACP) statistics
a1374.speech: "over 30,000 babies are born annually with HIV."

a1374.speaker: Dr Zainab Akol, Manager of the AIDS Control Programme (ACP)
a1374.speech: "was quoted at a recent function saying If urgent measures are not taken, we are losing out on the war against HIV/AIDS."

a1407.speaker: Elon Musk
a1407.speech: Announced the president's agreement to "put an end to" the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), during a conversation on X on Monday. "We have a ball of worms," Musk declared, comparing USAID to an "unfixable" and "incredibly partisan" institution ; denounces its support for "radically anti-American causes" ; proclaims "it's time for it to die."

a1407.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1407.speech: Described the agency on Sunday as being "run by a bunch of radical lunatics."

a1407.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a1407.speech: Sources mention threats of intervention by US Marshals to force the doors open, while DOGE demanded access to classified data and personnel files.

a1407.speaker: Katie Miller, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a1407.speech: Maintains that "no one consulted a classified document without authorization."

a1407.speaker: Democratic senators
a1407.speech: Are raising the alarm in a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, asserting that this incident raises deep concerns about national security.

a1407.speaker: Former senior USAID official (anonymous)
a1407.speech: "It's a dismantling in stages," he denounces, on condition of anonymity. "DOGE wants to absorb USAID, but the State Department has neither the expertise nor the culture to steer development projects." "We are scuttling a unique tool." ; "Without it, we will be striking with one arm behind our back," warns the former official.

a1407.speaker: Stephen Miller, US Deputy Chief of Staff
Senate Democrats
a1407.speech: Point out that Congress must approve any merger with the State Department, an institutional safeguard that the executive seems ready to defy.

a1501.speaker: AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) (announcement)
a1501.speech: will lead the 2nd Silent Protest in Durban on Friday 21 August 2015, demonstrating solidarity with rape survivors and demanding greater access to Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) after rape, in line with AHF's 20x20 Campaign. ; Stated the purposes of the protest: to raise awareness around the epidemic of rape in South Africa, highlighting the silence around sexual violence and the state's inability or unwillingness to support rape survivors; to demonstrate the connection between HIV and gender-based violence; to challenge the currently problematic implementation of the Sexual Offences Amendment Act as it relates to access to PEP; to stop victim-blaming; and to symbolise all rape survivors whose voices are silenced by rape.

a1501.speaker: South African Police Services (SAPS) crime statistics
a1501.speech: The latest available statistics, reported in 2013/14, reveal that 66 000 sexual assaults were reported in SA. Of these only 6.5% have been successfully prosecuted and less than half of 1% of perpetrators will serve any jail-time. ; The most shocking estimate of the ratio of reporting to non-reporting of rape survivors comes from the SAPS (1 in 25).

a1501.speaker: Rape Crisis
a1501.speech: provides the most conservative estimate of the ratio of reporting to non-reporting of rape survivors (1 in 4).

a1501.speaker: Diversity and Equality in Health and Care (journal; Nare, Prince, Volume 10, Number 4, December 2013)
a1501.speech: According to the journal, challenges obstructing access to PEP treatment within the crucial 72-hour time limit include lack of awareness about PEP among both survivors and professionals and the inability of individual provider institutions to meet patients' needs, especially in rural areas.

a1501.speaker: Deborah Birx, PEPFAR Global AIDS Coordinator
a1501.speech: noted that "with 7,000 new infections per week, young women in sub-Saharan Africa are an especially vulnerable population, and when mixing in the high prevalence of sexual violence, they are four times more likely to contract sexually transmitted infections."

a1501.speaker: Treatment Action Campaign
a1501.speech: states that to ensure that PEP treatment is effective and to prevent HIV infection after a rape incident, the survivor should start PEP treatment as soon as possible but no later than 72 hours after the rape or sexual assault; take every dose of the medication as prescribed for 28 days; be tested and treated for other sexually transmitted infections; be tested for pregnancy; practice safe sex for at least six months after the rape incident; and return to the health facility for follow-up tests and counselling at six weeks, three months, six months, and one year after the rape incident.

a1662.speaker: Trump administration
a1662.speech: Later clarified that essential services would continue while aid is reviewed.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee (communique of 16 October 2024)
a1685.speech: Revealed that on Domestic Macroeconomic Developments, the Quarterly Real GDP (QRGDP) improved by a growth of 1.3 percent relative to the contraction recorded in quarter two 2024. The Committee attributed this slight increase to the quarter-on-quarter moderation in consumer prices and improvement in consumption, and remains optimistic that economic activity will strengthen in the last quarter of the year on account of consumption and Government of Liberia fiscal impulse.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Expressed optimism about the moderation of inflation to 6.8 percent from 7.4 percent in the second quarter, noting that this development was due to improved food prices and CBL's policy stance. The Committee was also satisfied with the 2024 last quarter inflation forecast, expecting it to further moderate to 6.4 percent, within a symmetric band of +/- 2.0 percentage points.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Expressed concern about the performance of the banking system, observing that apart from slight growth in loans and advances, other key balance sheet items declined during the quarter, as total loans and advances rose by 1.2 percent while total assets, deposits and total capital declined by 0.6 percent, 2.6 percent and 1.6 percent respectively; and noted a 1.79 percentage points increase in non-performing loans (NPLs).

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Observed that loans and advances are mainly concentrated in five sectors: trade (28.6 percent); personal (16.6 percent); service (15.1 percent); oil & gas (8.3 percent); and construction (6.8 percent), and expressed concerns over the low intermediation by the banking system to the agriculture and manufacturing subsectors, also noting that these five sectors recorded the highest share of NPLs.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Noted that credit to the private sector showed mixed results in both currencies: the Liberian dollar component was down by 0.9 percent to L$5.79 billion from L$5.85 billion, mainly due to contractions in credit advanced to agriculture, services and manufacturing, while USD credits to the private sector rose by 1.3 percent to US$481.6 million from US$475.6 million, largely on account of growth in credits to services and agriculture.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Noted that monetary aggregates recorded slight declines in quarter three 2024, with broad money (M2) down 1.6 percent and currency in circulation contracting by 0.1 percent to L$27.69 billion. The Committee was satisfied with the moderation of monetary aggregates and expressed concern that the last quarter would record growth in these aggregates, especially currency outside banks, that could engender exchange rate and inflationary pressures.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Noted that activity in the financial markets was relatively positive for the CBL bills and the interbank market, though there was no government market activity during the period; total subscriptions to CBL bills rose by 24.8 percent, and nine USD SWAPS transactions valued at US$8.86 million were made at a weighted average interest rate of 1.375 percent. The Committee noted the absence of Government treasury bills activity in the market, describing this as a potential risk to financial markets development.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Observed that government fiscal operations resulted in a deficit during quarter three of 2024, largely on account of a 0.5 percent reduction in expenditure coupled with a 9.7 percent reduction in revenue, though Primary Balances recorded a surplus of US$4.8 million. The Committee was concerned that the quarter ahead could see a significant rise in government spending, potentially increasing the risk of exchange rate and inflation uncertainties.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Was encouraged by the resilience of the global economy, noting that it avoided a recession in 2023 and achieved real GDP growth of 3.3 percent, and expressing optimism that the growth projection of 3.2 percent for 2024 is attainable; observed that projected growth of 1.7 percent in advanced economies suggests a moderate recovery and that Sub-Saharan Africa growth is expected to accelerate to 3.7 percent from 3.4 percent in 2023. It acknowledged the downward trajectory of global headline inflation to 5.9 percent from 6.7 percent, while observing that inflation remains high in several low-income countries, particularly the Sub-Saharan region, where it is expected to moderate to 15.3 percent from 16.2 percent.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Observed an increase in commodity prices during the quarter, driven mainly by agriculture, with rising prices of cocoa, palm oil and round logs while rice and coffee prices declined; in metals and energy only gold recorded a rise, while iron ore and petroleum prices declined, and the decline in petroleum prices partly helped to improve the trade deficit for the quarter.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Recognized the significant improvement in the trade deficit to a projection of US$48.9 million from US$168.3 million in quarter two 2024, attributed to a 22.3 percent reduction in import payments and a 2.5 percent rise in merchandise export receipts, and observed that gross international reserves rose by an estimated 6.5 percent, raising months of essential imports cover to 2.9 from 2.2.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee
a1685.speech: Was satisfied with exchange rate movements for quarter three, noting that the Liberian dollar on an end-period basis remained relatively stable, marginally appreciating by 0.59 percent to L$193.26/US$1.00 at end-September 2024 compared to L$194.39/US$1.00 at end-June 2024, while on an average basis it marginally depreciated by 0.68 percent. The Committee remains confident that relative stability in the exchange rate will continue in the next quarter, anchored on effective liquidity management.

a1685.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia Monetary Policy Committee (decisions)
a1685.speech: Decided to lower the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 17.0 percent, consistent with the expectation of moderation in consumer prices and a stable exchange rate, and to maintain the reserve requirement ratios of 25 percent and 10 percent for Liberian and US dollars respectively until the next quarter's assessment. In conclusion, the CBL Committee reassured the public that "we will continue to monitor developments in both the domestic and global economies in accordance with our mandate and implement policies that enhance macroeconomic stability of the Liberian economy."

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Proposed in his budget speech that all employees who receive a monthly pay not exceeding D3000 are free from payment of income tax, effective 1st January 2025; informed that in addition to tax policy and revenue administration reforms, the Government is seeking to introduce further revenue measures effective 1st January 2025, with proposed income tax rates of 0 per cent on chargeable income of D36,000 or less, 5 per cent from D36,001 to D46,000, 10 per cent from D46,001 to D56,000, 15 per cent from D56,001 to D66,000, 20 per cent from D66,000 to D76,000 and 25 per cent above D76,000.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Said that a person who retains the services of a supplier, consultant, contractor or subcontractor shall withhold tax on the gross amount of any payment, at the rate of 10 per cent for a non-resident contractor, 5 per cent for a resident contractor for public works contracted with the Government of The Gambia, and 8 per cent in any other case; said that "A tenant, who is a Ministry, Government department or agency, local authority, diplomatic mission, international organization, established entities or a person under the category of large 43 taxpayers occupying a property used for commercial or residential purposes shall at the time of making payments withhold tax on the rental income at the rate of 15 percent in the case of a property used for commercial purpose, and 8 percent in the case of a property used for residential purposes."

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Reported that a non-resident person who makes a taxable supply to The Gambia shall register for tax with the Authority and obtain a Tax Identification Number, shall include the tax on its invoice for all taxable supplies, that the person to whom a taxable supply is made shall withhold or collect the tax and remit it to the Gambia Revenue Authority in the currency of the transaction, that a non-resident person may appoint a representative for compliance purposes, and that the Gambia Revenue Authority may issue guidelines including the form, time and procedure for filing returns and payment by non-resident suppliers; said non-resident suppliers of online or digital business-to-consumer and business-to-business goods or services shall register with and obtain a Tax Identification Number from the Gambia Revenue Authority, and that the Commissioner General shall prescribe the type of documents that may be transmitted to the Authority by a non-resident person, including the manner of transmission.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Said the tax rate on the winnings of betting, gaming, lottery and gambling will be increased from thirty per cent to forty per cent of the winning, defining winnings as the payout from a betting, gaming, lottery, prize competition, gambling or similar transaction under the Betting and Gaming Act, excluding the amount staked or wagered.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Said that with the approval of the Director of Agriculture, animal feed and agricultural equipment shall be exempt from duty if the Minister responsible for Finance is satisfied that the items are for the sole use of poultry farming or agricultural purposes; said export duty shall be imposed on waste and scrap metals at the rate of D5 per kilo and the tobacco control levy on cigarettes, cigars and cigarillos is revised to D2 per kilo.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Detailed that excise tax on cigarettes and cigars is adjusted from D40/pack to D45/pack; environmental tax on cigarettes and cigars from D7.22/pack to D9.22/pack; excise tax on other tobacco products from D450/kg to D470/kg; environmental tax on other tobacco products from D220/kg to D240/kg; and the ad valorem excise tax on imported tobacco products from 10 per cent to 15 per cent; also indicated increments in excise taxes on alcohol: beer from D150 per litre to D165 per litre, wine from D225 per litre to D240 per litre and spirits from D260 per litre to D275 per litre.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Averred that motor vehicles purchased and imported by and in the name of the Government of the Gambia shall be exempt from all taxes and fees: "This exemption is only applicable to central government entities and excludes government agencies and public enterprises. Taxable supply of goods or services in respect of a donor-funded project shall be zero-rated for the purposes of Value Added Tax"; detailed that MDAs are required to submit to the MOFEA a list of all contractors and copies of contracts.

a1745.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister (budget speech)
a1745.speech: Said the sales/purchase of air tickets shall be subject to a withholding tax rate of one per cent, while abolishing the green tea tax; said that in order to promote youth and sports development in the country, companies and businesses will benefit from tax deductions during the computation of corporate income taxes for expenses arising from sports activities.

a1840.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a1840.speech: Claimed that USAID funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram, made during the inaugural hearing of the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency.

a1840.speaker: US Mission to Nigeria (post via X)
a1840.speech: Confirmed that monitoring systems are in place to track past assistance provided by the US government and strongly condemned the ongoing violence and loss of life caused by Boko Haram in Nigeria: "Comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems are in place to help verify that U.S. assistance reaches intended recipients. The United States condemns the violence and blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups in Nigeria and the region. ; The Secretary of State designated Boko Haram a Foreign Terrorist Organization on November 14, 2013 to block the organization's assets and fundraising efforts, prosecute individual members, and restrict their travel to the United States. The United States continues to work with Nigeria and regional partners to counter terrorism."

a1840.speaker: Ali Ndume, Senator representing Borno-South Senatorial District
a1840.speech: Voiced concerns about the claim that USAID financed terrorist groups, including Boko Haram, through annual funds amounting to $697 million, and urged the federal government to investigate what he described as a weighty allegation by the US Congressman, asking the federal government to ensure that the matter is not swept under the carpet.

a1840.speaker: Ali Ndume, Senator representing Borno-South Senatorial District
a1840.speech: Urged the Tinubu government to focus on becoming self-sufficient, rather than relying on foreign aid.

a1840.speaker: General Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a1840.speech: Called on the United Nations to investigate the funding and training of the Boko Haram terrorists, saying there was international flow of funding for the terrorists and stressing the need for the UN to come in to trace and track it: "The problem is that I think we have talked to the international community. Let's find out the funding. As we speak, over 120,000 Boko Haram members have surrendered, and most of them came with hard currency. How did they get it? How are they funded? How did they get the training? How did they get the equipment? ; The UN needs to come in because we need to trace the funding. It is international flow, and we don't have control over that." ; Asked what his suspicion was: "Well, maybe an international conspiracy... How are they being able to sustain themselves for 15 years? That is one question I think everybody should ask themselves." He also said he did not know whose interest it is to see Nigeria destabilised.

a1840.speaker: Borno Elder Forum
a1840.speech: Has called on the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and other non-governmental organisations to leave Borno State and the North-east region.

a1840.speaker: Dr Bulama Male Gubio, Secretary of the Borno Elder Forum
a1840.speech: Appealed to the Nigerian government to allow US President Donald Trump to investigate the claim made by the Congressman: "I raised concern about the sinister activities of NGOs in Borno State in 2014. I was invited to Abuja and detained for questioning. It took the intervention of Borno elders to bail me out."

a2051.speaker: Jack Allison, former Peace Corps volunteer in Malawi (1967-69) and music diplomat
a2051.speech: “From a lifetime of practicing music diplomacy, I urge that music be highlighted as a powerful means of promulgating peace and goodwill.” ; “Music diplomacy is essential at a time like this to be utilized whenever possible to foster peace and crosscultural sharing for the common good.”

a2601.speaker: Ato Tewodros Getachew, President of the Federal Bar Association and Vice President of the Pan African Lawyers Union (Ethiopian candidate)
a2601.speech: Lodged a complaint saying the COMESA judges’ recruitment competition “is not fair”, and filed a claim saying “The Mauritian candidate should be cancelled from the competition and I should become a judge of the COMESA Court of Justice”; said he submitted the appeal because the selection of the COMESA Court of Justice judges did not follow the procedure issued by the institution and raises a question of fairness.

a2601.speaker: Ato Tewodros Getachew, Ethiopian candidate for the COMESA Court of Justice
a2601.speech: Told The Reporter that he is attending and participating in person in the proceedings in Lusaka, and explained that in the litigation so far the comments presented by the COMESA Secretary General, the COMESA Council of Ministers and the Mauritian-national candidate judge regarding the selection of judges were rejected by the court.

a2601.speaker: David Sigano, executive of the East Africa Law Society
a2601.speech: Said in an email reply to The Reporter: “We wanted to take part in the litigation process on the selection of the judges of the COMESA Court of Justice in order to see the transparency of the institution’s selection of judges.”

a2601.speaker: COMESA Court of Justice (ruling)
a2601.speech: Gave a unanimous decision on the evening of Friday Ginbot 22, 2017 E.C. that the injunction should continue, rejected the request by the COMESA Secretary General and the COMESA Council of Ministers that the appointment injunction be partially lifted, and ruled that the case and evidence be heard on 03 June 2025.

a2601.speaker: Diplomat at Ethiopia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (anonymous)
a2601.speech: Told The Reporter that COMESA has, as far as it has been able, been arranging that Ethiopia should not take part in its meetings and that its voice should not be heard; said the organisation is run under the dominance of certain countries that do not want Ethiopia’s interests, and that as a founding country Ethiopia must exert pressure in a coordinated manner to protect its interests.

a2601.speaker: Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia (Ethiopia’s national focal point at COMESA)
a2601.speech: Stated that it has no information about the litigation taking place in Lusaka.

a2601.speaker: Yasmin Wohabrebbi, State Minister of Trade and Regional Integration
a2601.speech: “Various efforts are being made to protect Ethiopia’s interests in COMESA. I know that other Ethiopians have participated in the COMESA Court of Justice before. But I do not know about the matter connected with Tewodros Getachew.”

a2601.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister of Finance
a2601.speech: Said recently, when he appeared before the House of People’s Representatives, that Ethiopia holds a large share in the COMESA Bank.

a2601.speaker: COMESA (non-response)
a2601.speech: The effort made to include COMESA’s response on the selection of the judges of the Court of Justice and on the complaint that it sidelines Ethiopia was not successful.

a2881.speaker: Hon. Justice Solomy Bossa, Chairperson of the Governing Council of ACDHRS
a2881.speech: Commended both the center and partner NGOs for the instrumental roles they continue to play in the realization, promotion, and protection of human rights in Africa. She said the work requires determination, commitment, and perseverance because it entails collaborative efforts with individuals, organizations, and governments to make an impact ; she added that by optimally deploying mega resources to seminars, workshops, and research to provide documentation and publication, and by focusing on contemporary human rights issues, the center has realized the vision of its founders ; she implored the respective governments in Africa not to derail NGOs and not to view them as detractors, because their work entails exposing gaps and shortcomings in the enforcement of human rights.

a2881.speaker: Foluso Adegalu, representative of the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions (NANHRI)
a2881.speech: Said education is key to fostering meaningful participation in economic development, particularly within frameworks such as the Africa Continental Free Trade (ACFT). He said through human rights education, individuals can be equipped with the knowledge necessary to advocate for equitable access to the benefits of the ACFT area ; he went on to state that by emphasizing human rights on the continent, they would ensure that marginalized communities are not left behind in the distribution of economic property indices ; as a network, he said they would always emphasize the critical role that national human rights institutions play in advancing and promoting human rights and accountability.

a2881.speaker: Dabasaki Mac-Ikemenjima, Ford Foundation, representative of the partners of ACDHRS
a2881.speech: Said the continent is in a moment of urgency. He said the work they do now is more critical and important than at any other time in the history of the region ; "The region faces many challenges such as economic, political, security and social. This moment requires us to rethink, re-adjust, and re-imagine the way we do our work" ; some of these challenges, he added, include the trend of democratic backsliding, the closing of civil space, and rising taxation within states in the region ; "As we know, our region faces an increasing trend of military overthrows. In West Africa alone, we have four countries that are currently under military rule, and there have been attempts at overthrowing a civilian government in several countries, that have not been successful. These moments require their re-thinking of our strategies and approaches to address issues of human rights on the continent."

a2881.speaker: Hon. Justice Raymond Sock, former Executive Director of the Center (ACDHRS)
a2881.speech: Said in pursuit of their objective, they have over the years physically considered issues that are of critical relevance to the situation of human rights in Africa. One such issue he said is on the theme called: "Year of Education: Educate an Africa fit for the 21st Century: Building Resilient Education Systems for Increased Access to Inclusive, Lifelong Quality and Relevant Learning in Africa." The forum he said is a continuation of the discussion preceding the 79th Ordinary Session of the Africa Commission in May 2024 ; he said the UN General Assembly on the 19th of December 2011, adopted the declaration on human rights education which said human rights education should be available, accessible, acceptable, and of good quality.

a2894.speaker: Antoine Lavoisier
a2894.speech: Said: nothing is lost, nothing is created, everything is transformed (“rien ne se perd, rien ne se crée, tout se transforme”).

a2894.speaker: Presidential decree of Djibouti (20 April 2016)
a2894.speech: In Djibouti, a presidential decree on the importation and marketing of non-biodegradable bags and packaging was issued on 20 April 2016.

a2974.speaker: Meta (company statement)
a2974.speech: Said it detected little impact of artificial intelligence across its platforms this year; Meta says its defences were able to prevent AI-driven misinformation operations from gaining an online foothold; in 2024, Meta says it ran several election operations centres around the world to monitor content issues, including during elections in the US, Bangladesh, Brazil, France, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan, South Africa, the United Kingdom and the European Union; in the month leading up to Election Day in the US, Meta said it rejected 590,000 requests to generate images of President Joe Biden, then-Republican candidate Donald Trump and his running mate, JD Vance, Vice President Kamala Harris and Governor Tim Walz.

a2974.speaker: Nick Clegg, Meta president of global affairs
a2974.speech: Told reporters on Tuesday that the limited impact was in part due to defensive measures designed to prevent coordinated networks of accounts, or bots, from grabbing attention on Facebook, Instagram and Threads ; “I don’t think the use of generative AI was a particularly effective tool for them to evade our trip wires,” Clegg said of actors behind coordinated disinformation campaigns ; Said overall, the volume of AI-generated misinformation was low and Meta was able to quickly label or remove the content, despite 2024 being the biggest election year ever, with some 2 billion people estimated to have gone to the polls around the world ; “People were understandably concerned about the potential impact that generative AI would have on elections during the course of this year” ; In a statement, he said that “any such impact was modest and limited in scope”, adding that AI content, such as deepfake videos and audio of political candidates, was quickly exposed and failed to fool public opinion.

a2974.speaker: Nick Clegg, Meta president of global affairs
a2974.speech: Said most of the covert influence operations it has disrupted in recent years were carried out by actors from Russia, Iran and China, adding that Meta took down about 20 “covert influence operations” on its platform this year; Russia was the number one source of those operations, with 39 networks disrupted in total since 2017, followed by Iran with 31, and China with 11.

a2974.speaker: Nick Clegg, Meta president of global affairs (and others)
a2974.speech: Have warned that disinformation has moved to social media and messaging websites not owned by Meta, especially TikTok, where some studies have found evidence of fake AI-generated videos featuring politically related misinformation.

a2974.speaker: Bruce Schneier and Nathan Sanders, Harvard academics (article in The Conversation, ‘The apocalypse that wasn’t’)
a2974.speech: “There was AI-created misinformation and propaganda, even though it was not as catastrophic as feared.”

a2974.speaker: Pew survey of Americans
a2974.speech: In a Pew survey of Americans earlier this year, nearly eight times as many respondents expected AI to be used for mostly bad purposes in the 2024 election as those who thought it would be used mostly for good.

a2974.speaker: Joe Biden, US President (national security memorandum on AI)
a2974.speech: In October, Biden rolled out new plans to harness AI for national security as the global race to innovate the technology accelerates; Biden outlined the strategy in a first-ever AI-focused national security memorandum (NSM) on Thursday, calling for the government to stay at the forefront of “safe, secure and trustworthy” AI development.

a2974.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a2974.speech: Earlier this year, Human Rights Watch accused Meta of silencing pro-Palestine voices amid increased social media censorship since October 7.

a2974.speaker: Meta (policy statement)
a2974.speech: Says its platforms were mostly used for positive purposes in 2024, to steer people to legitimate websites with information about candidates and how to vote; while it said it allows people on its platforms to ask questions or raise concerns about election processes, “we do not allow claims or speculation about election-related corruption, irregularities, or bias when combined with a signal that content is threatening violence”.

a2974.speaker: Nick Clegg, Meta president of global affairs
a2974.speech: Said the company was still feeling the pushback from its efforts to police its platforms during the COVID-19 pandemic, resulting in some content being mistakenly removed ; “We feel we probably overdid it a bit” ; “While we’ve been really focusing on reducing prevalence of bad content, I think we also want to redouble our efforts to improve the precision and accuracy with which we act on our rules.”

a2974.speaker: Some Republican lawmakers in the US
a2974.speech: Have questioned what they say is censorship of certain viewpoints on social media.

a2974.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a2974.speech: Has been especially critical, accusing its platforms of censoring conservative viewpoints.

a2974.speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta CEO (August letter to the US House of Representatives Judiciary Committee)
a2974.speech: Said he regretted some content take-downs the company made in response to pressure from the Biden administration.
