a6775.speech: Argues that the United States stands to lose far more from the foreign aid freeze than its 1% government investment in foreign aid: "Spending on biosecurity is an investment in the future - I think the United States benefits much more from our research and our work than what we cost them." ; "It's of great interest to America to keep investing - not as a kind of donation, or because we're entitled to it - but because of how it helps them. We just came out of a pandemic, and America actually had much bigger waves of infection than many of the poor countries."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: Insists that cross-border scientific collaboration is critical for combating the global spread of disease: "Pathogens don't need passports; they don't care about nationality."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: Lists recent global population health threats: "Like with Covid, now we have influenza; and the virus is mutating, transmitting through multiple animals. We just had an outbreak of Marburg in Rwanda and another one in Kenya. We had an emergence of mpox in central Africa. We had an emergence in Sudan of a strain of Ebola. In Uganda, there is a growing rate of malaria drug resistance." ; "And in the last year, the US saw the biggest number of TB cases ever. So it's of critical interest that these pathogens get quickly identified, are quickly controlled, that you treat people so that it doesn't spread to other countries." ; "In the end, it's the health of the global population; it doesn't matter which country we live in or how wealthy people are."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: Says only 7% of CERI's funding is from the NIH - "and we have reason to believe that the current NIH grants that we have will not be discontinued" - and says CERI and the KwaZulu-Natal Research Innovation and Sequencing Platform (KRISP) are expanding: "Yes, the opposite, we're in an expansion phase" ; "Just last week, we advertised five post-doctoral fellowship positions. We hope that we can even absorb some of the great talent that may be lost from groups that were unfortunately more reliant on American funding."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: Stresses the importance of having a diversified funding portfolio, saying the work of CERI and KRISP is funded through 46 active grants with another nine in the works: "We have multiple grants from multiple funders from multiple countries. So again, I know it's easily said, but I think it's something that we should learn going forward, not to grow too reliant on one funder."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: On who might fill the funding gap: "China could fill the gap. But people don't realise the biggest foundation in the world at the moment is called the Novo Nordisk Foundation in Denmark, which is linked to the company that had the massive breakthrough with Ozempic. They could easily fill the gap if they wanted. There are others as well. I would not be surprised if a completely unexpected foundation came forward to fill the gap." ; expresses hope that "people with noble causes step up."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: Says he feels "eternally grateful" for the boost Pepfar brought to South Africa's HIV programme, adding that today the country might be in a "better position to absorb the loss of the funding than say five, 10 years ago"; notes that 17% of South Africa's HIV/AIDS spending was from Pepfar, but that this does not include the procurement of antiretrovirals: "So yes, I think as South Africans, we might be in a position to come up with solutions, as the programme is very well run." Says his concern is for more vulnerable African countries - singling out Mozambique - which are reliant on foreign aid for the procurement of medicines like antiretrovirals.

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: On the impact on HIV vaccine research: "When you decrease investment in research and science, you keep further away from developing the solutions" ; "But in terms of HIV/AIDS, luckily, there are antiretroviral therapies that are very efficient."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: On the bigger picture: "Unfortunately, we are destroying the environment, there's increased globalisation and crazy urbanisation, and this is making it easier for infectious diseases to spread." ; "This is a challenging time for scientific and medical research. A time to develop solutions."

a6775.speaker: Tulio de Oliveira, Professor of bioinformatics and founding director of CERI, Stellenbosch University
a6775.speech: In a moment of levity: "And this is the fifth time I cracked my ribs. Once was while skateboarding, another while snowboarding, surfing, once while mountain biking and another time falling from a children's tractor."

a6775.speaker: Pew Research Center (non-partisan research organisation)
a6775.speech: Recently released figures showing that of the US government's total 2023 budget, 1.2%, or about $71.9 billion, was spent on foreign aid; of this foreign aid budget, 14.7%, or about $10.6 billion, was earmarked for the "ongoing battle against HIV/AIDS" and 2%, or about $1.5 billion, for "combatting pandemic influenza and other emerging public health threats".

a6775.speaker: Margaret Chan, former World Health Organisation director-general
a6775.speech: First used the phrase "Pathogens don't need passports" at the 2007 World Health Assembly.

a6775.speaker: Ntobeko Ntusi, President of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a6775.speech: Told Spotlight that it would be catastrophic if the US government funding - around 28% of the SAMRC's 2025/26 budget - was cut.

a6775.speaker: Robert F Kennedy, US health secretary
a6775.speech: Has argued that the NIH should reduce its focus on infectious diseases and dedicate more resources to non-communicable diseases like diabetes.

a6775.speaker: Clemence Landers, vice-president of the think tank Centre for Global Development (quoted in The New Yorker)
a6775.speech: Suggested that China might come forward to fill the gap if the United States pulls back permanently from its leadership role in providing global aid and medical research funding.

a6783.speaker: Juol Nhomngek, national lawmaker representing Cueibet County, Lakes State, South Sudan
a6783.speech: Described as unacceptable the recent increase in telecommunications tariffs, adding that the measure will contribute to denying citizens the right of access to information; said he is opposed to the move and urged the government to subsidize telecommunication services: "I would like to appeal to the public that I am against the increment. Because, the government must ensure that this services of the internet and plus other communication services are subsided" ; "The companies are taking advantage of the issue of dollar and we have our Pound we need to strengthen the value of our currency and prioritize the use of local currency instead of dollars." ; "So, when you look at the telecommunications sector, increasing their tariff repeatedly, time after time, now the citizens are really tired. This is unacceptable, and we cannot accept it." ; "I am not comfortable seeing the telecom sector increasing tariffs within a very short period. It is the duty of the government to ensure that services offered by providers are cheaper and affordable to the citizens."

a6783.speaker: Juol Nhomngek, national lawmaker representing Cueibet County, Lakes State, South Sudan
a6783.speech: Stated that lawmakers are awaiting the outcomes of the investigation committee established by parliament to investigate the alleged abnormal charges imposed on subscribers: "Up to now, the investigation is still ongoing because we have a budget that has interrupted it. The law says that when there is a budget in place, no other activities can take place until the findings are presented after the budget."

a6783.speaker: Zain, MTN and Digitel, mobile telecom operators (joint statement)
a6783.speech: Announced a three-phase increment in telecommunication costs from October to December, saying the tariff adjustments were made following an agreement with the National Communication Authority and the Bank of South Sudan, in response to the recent increase in the official exchange rate, and that the decision was reached following a thorough analysis of its potential impact on customers and the telecommunication sector.

a6845.speaker: Heads of State and government at the XIXth Francophonie Summit (4-5 October 2024, Paris)
a6845.speech: Calling for peace, expressed their concerns regarding several ongoing conflicts in Africa and their serious humanitarian repercussions.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: On Sudan: called for an immediate ceasefire and unhindered access for humanitarian aid in the conflict between the Sudanese armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces, which has caused a genuine humanitarian catastrophe; also stressed the importance of including civilians in the peace process in order to facilitate the democratic transition.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: On East Africa: condemns the violence against civilians and the attacks perpetrated by non-state armed groups that hinder the return to peace.

a6845.speaker: Member States of the OIF
a6845.speech: Call for the withdrawal of unauthorised foreign forces and support regional peace efforts.

a6845.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a6845.speech: Has repeatedly accused Rwanda of contributing to the deterioration of security in eastern DRC.

a6845.speaker: Global Terrorism Index
a6845.speech: Ranked Burkina Faso in 2022 as the country most affected by terrorism.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: On Burkina Faso: worried by the insecurity combined with a prolonged five-year transition, calls on the Burkinabè government to speed up the return to constitutional order and to guarantee citizens' rights.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: On Mali: calls for the organisation of swift elections to restore constitutional order in a country beset by terrorist attacks and delays in its electoral process.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: On Niger: demands free and transparent elections to restore democracy and calls for the immediate release of President Mohamed Bazoum.

a6845.speaker: La Francophonie (OIF)
a6845.speech: Reaffirms its commitment to supporting peace, democracy and human rights in Africa, while urging the international community to step up its efforts to resolve these conflicts and improve the humanitarian situation.

a6855.speaker: Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL)
a6855.speech: “Clearly, President Boakai can boast of relative success in other areas, but not in the fight against corruption, Liberia’s biggest problem.”

a6855.speaker: Anderson Miamen, Executive Director, CENTAL
a6855.speech: Said in a live Facebook podcast that the President has been lackluster when it comes to taking action on allegations of corruption against his officials, saying “He has not really matched his anti-corruption commitments with deeds.” ; argues that President Boakai removed the entire board of commissioners at LTA because of allegations of corruption, but has taken no action against the current acting LTA board chair, who is implicated in an audit report released by the General Auditing Commission; wonders what the President has done to his officials who have refused to declare their assets: “He keeps giving them warning and ultimatum. What has he done to Dorr Cooper investigated by the University of Liberia and found liable for academic fraud? Again, nothing. I could go on and on.” ; “Like Weah, President Boakai is not doing enough to send a strong message to his officials to comply with the Code of Conduct and other Anti-Corruption laws. We can’t compare CDC’s six years to UP’s one year. However, we can speak to the trends and what likely will happen, should things change or continue the way they are.”

a6855.speaker: Anderson Miamen, Executive Director, CENTAL
a6855.speech: According to him, former President Weah and his party lost the 2023 presidential election not necessarily because they did not build roads or other public facilities; mainly, they lost because they failed to deal with corruption.

a6855.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia (state of the nation address)
a6855.speech: Outlined progress in key sectors such as the economy, infrastructure, agriculture, and education; addressed Liberia’s economic challenges before he assumed office, noting that the economy had grown by only 4.6%, inflation had surged to 10.1%, and the country’s debt burden had escalated to $2.5 billion; highlighted struggles faced by civil servants, particularly pay harmonization and delayed salary payments; revealed that decisive actions have been implemented, including salary increases for health workers, police officers, and teachers, and reported that in 2024 Liberia’s economy showed resilience with a revised GDP growth rate of 5.1%, growth fuelled by mining, agriculture, fisheries and services, with international partners like the World Bank, the African Development Bank, and USAID contributing to investments in infrastructure and energy development. “We have managed inflation prudently, reducing it to 7.7% by the end of 2024, down from 10.1% in 2023. We expect inflation to decrease further to 6.0% in 2025.” He also pointed to improvements in Liberia’s international reserves, which have risen to $458.9 million, appreciation of the Liberian dollar by 4.7% against the US dollar, and the Central Bank’s lowering of the monetary policy rate from 20% to 17%, which helped bolster confidence in the financial system and resulted in a 9.1% increase in private sector credit.

a6855.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia (state of the nation address)
a6855.speech: On infrastructure, highlighted several key projects, including the expansion of the Roberts International Airport (RIA) Road Project from 8 to 20 kilometres of paved road, as well as significant progress on the Sanniquellie to Logatuo and Saclepea to Tappita road projects; mentioned road development funded by the World Bank’s Rural Economic Transformation Project (RETRAP).

a6855.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia (state of the nation address)
a6855.speech: In the education sector, acknowledged the challenges his administration inherited, including $2 million in scholarship arrears, poorly qualified teachers, and inadequate infrastructure; said his government allocated $1 million to clear scholarship arrears, including WASSCE fees, and launched a $75 million foundational learning project with USAID to improve literacy and math skills for third-grade students.

a6855.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia (state of the nation address)
a6855.speech: In the health sector, touted the progress made under his ARREST Agenda, reporting reductions in maternal and child mortality rates and an increase in child vaccination rates from 64.9% to 73% in 2024.

a7012.speaker: Pascaline Barankeba, IFAD Country Director
a7012.speech: Speaking at the workshop, said that for many years IFAD has remained a steadfast and committed partner to Liberia's development goal, specifically significantly contributing to agriculture revitalization; said the new strategic framework for the country will ensure consolidation of achievements and lessons from past interventions in line with the policies and strategies for the country's agriculture ; "Let us challenge ourselves to think differently, act strategically, and commit to delivering an innovative, inclusive, and ambitious yet practical COSOP that will uplift rural farmers, empower women and youth, people with disabilities, and indigenous populations, and contribute to a food-secure and resilient Liberia where the private sector should play a critical role."

a7012.speaker: David Akoi, Deputy Agriculture Minister for Planning and Development
a7012.speech: Said that the Government of Liberia is grateful to IFAD and other international partners for their assistance in supporting the agricultural sector. "With support provided by the government projects, some of the young people have taken advantage of the sector to improve their lives."

a7012.speaker: Dehpue Duo, Deputy Finance Minister for Economic Management
a7012.speech: Said the IFAD project will help address the gap in the agriculture sector, which came as the result of USAID's cut for agriculture.

a7097.speaker: Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Disaster Risk Management Commission of Ethiopia
a7097.speech: Told Capital that the Commission is preparing to purchase one million metric tons of wheat through three phases: "The procurement process will be based on the international wheat market and by our 2021 need," adding "since the global market is changing we made the procurement through three phases" ; Said the commission has planned to commence two of the phases through direct procurement as 'urgent procurement' due to the current situation in the country, while the remaining phase will be procured through the Public Procurement and Property Disposal Service (PPPDS).

a7097.speaker: Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Disaster Risk Management Commission of Ethiopia
a7097.speech: Said the Commission is working to identify the total humanitarian assistance needed in the country, and that due to the military offence in the Tigray region, including some 1.1 million people who were getting food aid under the safety net program, it is estimated that there are about 1.8 million in need of humanitarian assistance ; "The internal displacement in the region is not that much; therefore it does not affect the normal operation of the commission that much" ; Said that by deploying eight coordination teams the Commission dispatched food and non-food assistance to 250,000 people in Tigray region as soon as the military operation ended, and that so far 70 trucks of humanitarian aid had been sent to the region to supply both food and non-food items.

a7097.speaker: National Disaster and Risk Management Commission (public assurance)
a7097.speech: "The Ethiopian government has provided the Tigray population with food and other staples, within the rehabilitation process of the regional state," the Commission assured the public on Thursday.

a7097.speaker: Official sources
a7097.speech: According to official sources, several non-governmental agencies are also providing humanitarian assistance, including agriculture and livestock, water and sanitation, health, education and nutrition, non-food items, logistics and different sanitary products for women and children.

a7122.speaker: Aklilu Tadesse, CEO of the Industrial Parks Development Corporation (IPDC)
a7122.speech: Aklilu said service delivery improvements have greatly increased the investment flow in the parks last year with 5,000 job opportunities expected to be open through this investment.

a7122.speaker: International Trade Portal
a7122.speech: According to the International Trade Portal, FDI inflows to Ethiopia increased to 4.2 billion dollars in 2021, up from 2.4 billion dollars the previous year.

a7180.speaker: Executives of Multiverse Enterprise Plc and Addis Abeba Minibus Associations
a7180.speech: According to executives, the Enterprise has secured enough foreign currency to import parts from King Long, a Chinese manufacturer, to be locally assembled by the Defense Engineering Industry Corporation (DEIC).

a7180.speaker: Addis Abeba Minibus Association members
a7180.speech: have voiced infrastructural and financial constraints [regarding the ordered transition from associations to commercial entities].

a7218.speech: Just a few years ago, some experts estimated illegally-traded rhino horn to be of higher value by weight than either gold or cocaine at $65,000 per kilogramme in consumer markets.

a7218.speaker: Gordon Brown, former British Prime Minister
a7218.speech: Compared financial information and forensic accounting to the impact fingerprints and DNA brought about in criminal investigations in previous centuries.

a7218.speaker: Recent estimates (cited)
a7218.speech: Recent estimates have put the economy of money laundering at around 2-5 per cent of global GDP, or in the trillions of US dollars.

a7437.speaker: Students of political science / one pundit (anonymous)
a7437.speech: Posit that the entire national governance ecosystem is crumbling in effect if not already crumbled, as the sister wing of Senate constitutionally can hardly do anything with the House, and as neither the Executive nor the Judiciary can be considered wholesome-functionally relevant and effective; that Liberia is under siege, governance almost completely paralyzed at the behest of 73 Liberians who have chosen to do the work of their ego.

a7437.speaker: Governance experts that talked to The Analyst (anonymous)
a7437.speech: Said the political war on Capitol Hill has got crippling effects on the running of Liberia.

a7437.speaker: James Maston Toby, political activist
a7437.speech: "To understand the enormous consequences of what is happening on Capitol Hill, one needs to read Article 34 of our Constitution which places into the hands and care of the National Legislature the entire governance ecosystem of the country." ; "One of the most obvious hiccup looming as the result of the House imbroglio is the national budget process upon which the very survival of the government and the nation depends. Article 34 contains a bundle of critical prerogatives on the state's fiscal and monetary regimes, and much is left to desire what happens to these fiduciary actions of the Legislature in its current fragile state." ; recounted some of these constitutional actions - now in abeyance due to House infighting - as including the Legislature's right to levy taxes, duties, imports, exercise and other revenues, to borrow money, issue currency, mint coins, and to make appropriations for the fiscal governance of the Republic ; "Another key stake that is floating is the Legislature's key function of all revenue bills, whether subsidies, charges, imports, duties or taxes, and other financial bills that the constitution says shall originate in the House of Representatives."

a7437.speaker: Ocrates Keh
a7437.speech: "The House lawmakers are breaching critical prerogatives, and I am surprised they appear so oblivious if not ignorant of the magnitude of the problems they are causing the government and the state. The very security of the state, as articulated in Article 34(b) of the Constitution, lies with the Legislature. And the House is so cojoined with the Senate such that one wing cannot recess or adjourn without the consent of the other even for five days. I wonder if the House members know this-not only that their action and inaction imprison themselves, but also that consciously or unconsciously they have concurrently caved their Senate counterparts and the entire nation."

a7437.speaker: Shelton Z. Crayton, Jr., activist and political science student
a7437.speech: "This is in effect a coup against the state, and let's be clear and forceful about this." ; "A coup d'etat that targets the head of the Executive Branch is no less out of order and destabilizing than the one that targets the head of the Legislature or head of any of its wings. Whether it is the Executive, or the Judiciary or the Legislature that is decapitated or rendered ineffective to conduct its constitutional responsibilities, the fact is that it crumbles the entire government and the nation. It is an overstatement for one to say that the disruption of the activities of the Legislature is more treasonable and criminal in nature since the nation's political, social and economic life hangs on this branch of Government."

a7437.speaker: Shelton Z. Crayton, Jr., activist and political science student
a7437.speech: "It is unfortunate that the larger Liberian society, including the smarms of nongovernmental advocacy organizations, the religious community, constituencies of concerned lawmakers and all other relevant forces are treating the Capitol Hill debacle with demonstrated carelessness. Don't they know and realize that Liberia is paralyzed so long the Legislature or even a single wing thereof is paralyzed? Who's policing the acts of the Executive in these last months of the fiscal year? Who's keeping check on the Executive regarding its operations including but not limited to foreign, security, fiscal and monetary policies and operations? What's the fate of citizens whose representatives have abandoned their offices and relationships with them and are sleeping in hotels?"

a7437.speaker: Shelton Z. Crayton, Jr., student activist (speaking on a local radio live talk show)
a7437.speech: "These are critical issues to consider but it appears the nation is snoring on them. Already, civil servants are not taking pay regularly. Already, there is not a single groundbreaking, let alone dedication, of a single government-sponsored project. Millions of offshore monies are generated daily. In fact, the LRA has reported huge revenue intakes, surpassing targets, more than this same period of last year. Who knows and who is checking the Executive Branch on what's being done to the nation's huge revenue collection particularly during these last weeks - last minute expenditures - at the end of the 2024 fiscal period?"

a7437.speaker: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a7437.speech: Has reported huge revenue intakes, surpassing targets, more than this same period of last year.

a7437.speaker: Spokespersons of the University of Liberia's student leaderships and other young people in Monrovia
a7437.speech: Announced a series of actions to compel the lawmakers return to normal duties, including the mobilization of thousands of students and ordinary likeminded citizens to join them in protest against the virtual halt of legislative business in the country.

a7437.speaker: One of the students (University of Liberia campus-based spokesperson)
a7437.speech: "Our lawmakers are making fools out of us and it's time we showed them the people's power." ; "They are being paid taxpayers money-their monthly salaries and benefits are running unhindered while they are not doing the job for which they were elected and being paid lavishly by the Liberian people. This is criminal. It is labor theft. Secondly, why are these guys who are lawmakers refusing to abide by lawful precepts; why are they running away from the rule of law; why are they becoming breakers of laws?"

a7437.speaker: The other student activist (heard during the talk show)
a7437.speech: "But we have a message for the 43 lawmakers: return to business; return to work and you will be hooked out. If you don't want to work, if you don't know the importance of the job for which you were elected, quit. We are ready to mobilize as many Liberians as possible, and we will invade their offices, flush them outside and take over their seats. Lawlessness begets lawlessness. It is a revolution. It is the people's power." ; "Chapter I, Article I of our organic law, the 1986 Constitution, states and I quote: 'All power is inherent in the people. All free governments are instituted by their authority and for their benefit and they have the right to alter and reform the same when their safety and happiness so require...' We will fill those vacancies at the House of Representatives that are made void and dormant consciously by those lawmakers who voluntarily abandoned job, who refused High Court order to return to work, and who are using force and coercion to oust a colleague." ; "If 43 of them think they have power to arbitrary kick out a duly elected colleague, then it is appropriate and more honorable for thousands of Liberians to exercise a higher and more forceful power by kicking them out too."

a7437.speaker: 1986 Constitution of Liberia (Articles 3 and 34)
a7437.speech: Article 3 provides that Liberia is given to a Republican form of Government with three separate coordinate branches: the Legislative, the Executive and Judiciary, which consistent with the principles of separation of powers and checks and balances, bars a person holding office in one of these branches from holding office in or exercising any of the powers assigned to either of the other two branches.

a7437.speaker: J. Fonati Koffa, House Speaker
a7437.speech: Is rather requesting his day in court; that the petitioners should use the operating rules and laws appertaining to grievances including demands that he resigns.

a7437.speaker: 43 members of the House of Representatives
a7437.speech: Claiming majority power, are making demands for the resignation of their Speaker on account of violations they believe he has committed, and are boycotting sessions, refusing to sit under the gavel of their leader, until he resigns.
